verses.text: “Watch yourselves: don’t do good deeds in public just so people will notice. Do that, and your Father in heaven won’t reward you.

“When you give to people in need, don’t announce it with a trumpet like the hypocrites do in synagogues and on the streets to get people praising them. I’m telling you the truth: that applause is all the reward they’ll get.
“When you give, keep it so quiet your left hand doesn’t know what your right hand is doing.
“Let your giving stay private. Then your Father, who sees what happens in secret, will reward you openly.

“When you pray, don’t copy the hypocrites. They love standing in synagogues and street corners, praying where people can see them. I’m telling you the truth: that attention is all the reward they’ll get.
“But when you pray, go into your private room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is unseen. Your Father, who sees what happens in secret, will reward you openly.
“When you pray, don’t pile up empty phrases like the Gentiles do. They think all those words will make God hear them.
“Don’t copy them. Your Father already knows what you need before you ask him.
“Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
‘Let your Kingdom come. Let your will happen on earth just as it does in heaven.
‘Give us today the bread we need for today.
‘Forgive us for what we owe, just as we forgive those who owe us.
‘Don’t lead us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one. The Kingdom, the power, and the glory are yours forever. Amen.’
“If you forgive other people when they wrong you, your Father in heaven will forgive you too.
“But if you don’t forgive others when they wrong you, your Father won’t forgive your wrongs either.

“And when you fast, don’t pull a gloomy face like the hypocrites. They make themselves look miserable so people will know they’re fasting. I’m telling you the truth: that attention is all the reward they’ll get.
“But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
“so people won’t clock that you’re fasting—only your Father, who is unseen, will know. Your Father, who sees what happens in secret, will reward you openly.
“Don’t stack up treasures on earth, where moths and rust wreck them, and thieves break in and steal.
“Stack up treasures in heaven instead, where moths and rust can’t wreck them and thieves can’t break in and steal.
“Where your treasure is, your heart will be there too.
“The eye is the body’s lamp. If your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
“But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If the light inside you is darkness, that darkness is deep indeed.
“Nobody can serve two masters. You’ll hate one and love the other, or stay loyal to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
“So I’m telling you: don’t be anxious about your life—what you’ll eat or drink—or your body, what you’ll wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
“Look at the birds in the sky: they don’t plant, harvest, or store food in barns, yet your Father in heaven feeds them. Aren’t you worth much more than they are? 🐦
“Can any of you add even one moment to your life by worrying?
“And why stress about clothes? Look at the lilies in the field and how they grow. They don’t work hard or spin thread,
“yet I’m telling you, even Solomon in all his glory wasn’t dressed like one of them.
“If God dresses the field grass like this—here today, tossed into an oven tomorrow—won’t he clothe you even more, you of little faith?
“So don’t stress and ask, ‘What will we eat?’ ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’
“The Gentiles chase after all these things, but your Father in heaven knows you need them.
“Make God’s Kingdom and his righteousness your first pursuit, and all these things will be given to you too.
“So don’t stress about tomorrow. Tomorrow can deal with its own worries. Today already has enough trouble of its own.”
